# Task Tool Invocation

Subagent type: worker
Task complexity: heavy
Task description: Link PRs with gh stack

## Context
Use supplied context as authoritative. Do not repeat completed work or re-read supplied files unless writing them.
Stay within this assignment; if blocked, report the gap.

## Task
---BEGIN TASK FROM PARENT AGENT---
Use GitHub's `gh stack` extension (https://github.com/github/gh-stack) so the Effect PRs appear as a real GitHub stacked-PR object, not just PRs with chained bases.

WORK FROM: /root/hevy-mcp-effect-retry-interpreter (or a fresh worktree). Do NOT dirty /root/hevy-mcp user state (.pi-subagents, staged changeset).

INSTALL
```
gh extension install github/gh-stack
gh stack --help
```
If already installed, skip. Requires gh auth.

CURRENT OPEN PRs (chrisdoc/hevy-mcp)
Linear chain already using PR bases (but NOT a GitHub stack object, which is why the user cannot "see the stack"):
- #1104 feat/effect-pure-operations → main
- #1110 test/isolate-client-retry-schedule → feat/effect-pure-operations
- #1111 feat/effect-request-primitives → test/isolate-client-retry-schedule
- #1112 feat/effect-retry-interpreter → feat/effect-request-primitives

Still parallel on main (user asked to fix these):
- #1105 test/request-local-retry-state → main  (same tip 1c976a1 as #1109)
- #1109 test/fetch-config-merge → main (same tip)

INVESTIGATION ALREADY DONE
1105 and 1109 are THE SAME two commits: fa3fc92 (retry-schedule extract + small request-local tests) and 1c976a1 (fetch.test.ts config-merge characterization + lucky-pens-take changeset).
- retry-schedule.ts content is already on #1104/#1110/#1112
- 1110 has a BETTER/larger request-local-retry-state.test.ts and the real kubb isolation change
- UNIQUE leftover: packages/hevy-client/src/fetch.test.ts from 1c976a1
- Do NOT cherry-pick fa3fc92 onto 1112 (would collide with 1110 tests)
- Changeset lucky-pens-take.md may conflict; use a stack-appropriate non-empty changeset only if fetch.test.ts is a release trigger. Fetch characterization tests are often test-only; if check:changeset allows empty for test-only, do not add a bump. Follow repo AGENTS.md: test-only may use empty changeset ONLY if no packages/* runtime change. fetch.test.ts is tests — likely no bump needed.

WHAT TO DO

1. Install gh-stack. Run non-interactively wherever possible (`--auto`, `--open`, `--yes`). Do not hang on TUIs. If a command requires a TTY, use `gh stack link` which is designed for non-interactive linking of existing PRs.

2. Create the GitHub stack object for the Effect chain:
   ```
   gh stack link --open 1104 1110 1111 1112
   ```
   or equivalently by branch names in bottom-to-top order:
   ```
   gh stack link --open feat/effect-pure-operations test/isolate-client-retry-schedule feat/effect-request-primitives feat/effect-retry-interpreter
   ```
   Docs: gh stack link takes args bottom-to-top; creates/updates the GitHub stack; pushes branches; corrects PR bases; does not require local stack tracking.

3. Fix 1105: close it as superseded by #1110 (request-local characterization on the Effect stack). Use:
   `gh pr close 1105 --comment "..."`
   Do not delete the remote branch unless needed.

4. Fix 1109: keep the UNIQUE fetch.test.ts work.
   - Cherry-pick ONLY the fetch.test.ts change onto a NEW branch based on origin/feat/effect-retry-interpreter (top of stack). Do not include fa3fc92.
   - If cherry-pick of 1c976a1 is messy, extract just packages/hevy-client/src/fetch.test.ts.
   - Commit with Conventional Commit, Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com> if you make a new commit.
   - Push the new branch (never main, no --no-verify).
   - Append it to the GitHub stack:
     `gh stack link --open <existing-stack-number-or-1104> test/fetch-config-merge`
     OR `gh stack link --open 1104 1110 1111 1112 <new-branch>`
   - Then close the old #1109 if it still points at the duplicate 1c976a1 tip, OR retarget it if you reused the same branch name after rewriting. Prefer a NEW branch name like `test/fetch-config-merge-stack` to avoid force-pushing origin/test/fetch-config-merge.
   - If you must update origin/test/fetch-config-merge, do NOT force-push unless the branch would otherwise stay a parallel PR into main. Prefer new branch + close 1109.

5. After linking, verify the stack is visible:
   ```
   gh stack view
   gh pr list
   ```
   Also try GraphQL or `gh api` if needed to print the stack number and PR order.
   Open PR pages should show stacked-PR UI (stack number).

HARD RULES
- Never push to main. Never --no-verify.
- Avoid force-push of #1104/#1110/#1111/#1112.
- Avoid force-push of origin/test/fetch-config-merge and origin/test/request-local-retry-state if a new branch will do.
- Do not merge anything.
- All node/pnpm through mise if you run tests. Run focused fetch tests if you add fetch.test.ts.

OUTPUT (mandatory)
- gh-stack version / install result
- GitHub stack number if any
- Final PR order head→base with URLs
- What happened to 1105 and 1109
- Any force-push (branch + why)
- Commands that failed and how you worked around TTY

Do not write extra markdown files into the repo.
---END TASK FROM PARENT AGENT---
I'll work in the Effect retry worktree, install `gh-stack`, and link the existing PR chain without touching `/root/hevy-mcp`.

result.output:
Create or update a stack on GitHub from branch names, PR numbers, or PR URLs.

This command does not rely on gh-stack local tracking state. It is
designed for users who manage branches with external tools (e.g. jj,
Sapling, ghstack, git-town, etc...) and want to use GitHub stacked
PRs without adopting local stack tracking.

Arguments are provided in stack order (bottom to top). Each argument
can be a branch name, a PR number, or a PR URL (e.g.
https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123). For numeric arguments, the
command first checks if a PR with that number exists; if not, it
treats the argument as a branch name. PR URLs are always resolved
as pull requests (never as branch names).

Branch arguments are automatically pushed to the remote before
creating or looking up PRs. For branches that already have open PRs,
those PRs are used. For branches without PRs, new PRs are created
automatically with the correct base branch chaining.

If the PRs are not yet in a stack, a new stack is created. If some of
the PRs are already in a stack, the existing stack is updated to include
the new PRs (existing PRs are never removed).

As a shortcut for growing an existing stack, pass a stack number as the
first argument (the number shown in the GitHub stack UI). The remaining
arguments are appended to the top of that stack, so you don't have to
re-list its current PRs. Arguments already in the stack are skipped;
arguments that belong to a different stack are rejected. Because stack and
PR numbers never overlap, a numeric first argument is treated as a stack
only when it matches an existing stack.

Usage:
  gh stack link <stack-number | branch-or-pr> <branch-or-pr> [<branch-or-pr>...] [flags]

Examples:
  # Link branches into a stack (bottom to top)
  $ gh stack link auth-layer api-routes ui-components

  # Link existing PRs by number
  $ gh stack link 41 42 43

  # Link existing PRs by URL
  $ gh stack link https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/41 https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/42

  # Add PRs to the top of an existing stack (7 is a stack number)
  $ gh stack link 7 48 ui-polish

  # Specify a custom base branch for stack
  $ gh stack link --base develop auth-layer api-routes

Flags:
      --base string     Base branch for the bottom of the stack (defaults to the repository default branch)
  -h, --help            help for link
      --open            Mark new and existing PRs as ready for review
      --remote string   Remote to push to (defaults to auto-detected remote)
---
View the current stack as a list showing branches and PR status.

Status icons:
  ✓  PR merged
  ◎  PR queued
  ○  PR open
  ⚠  Needs rebase

The current branch is highlighted. Use --short for a compact one-line-per-branch
view, or --json for machine-readable output.

Usage:
  gh stack view [flags]

Examples:
  # Show the stack (default interactive view)
  $ gh stack view

  # Show compact output
  $ gh stack view --short

  # Output as JSON
  $ gh stack view --json

Flags:
  -h, --help    help for view
      --json    Output stack data as JSON
  -s, --short   Show compact output
